A student compared the stain-removing effects of several laundry detergents through an experiment (the more “+”, the better the stain-removing effect), and the experimental results are shown in the table below. Answer the question: What enzyme is added to enzyme-added laundry detergent C?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The columns in the table in the figure are enzyme-added laundry detergent A, enzyme-added laundry detergent B, enzyme-added laundry detergent C, and enzyme-free laundry detergent (control), and the rows include blood stain and oil stain. In the blood stain row, A is “+++”, B is “+”, C is “+++”, and the control is “+”; in the oil stain row, A is “+”, B is “+++”, C is “+++”, and the control is “+”. Then reason: The question stem states that the more “+”, the better the stain-removing effect. C has a removal effect of “+++” on both blood stains and oil stains, indicating that it can both effectively decompose protein in blood stains and effectively decompose fat in oil stains. Blood stains mainly correspond to protein and require protease; oil stains mainly correspond to fat and require lipase. Therefore, what is added to enzyme-added laundry detergent C is protease and lipase.
